fee.rule: 9% new construction: developer fee limited to the lesser of 13% of total development cost (excluding developer fee and reserves), $2,700,000, or $38,000 per unit (2026-2027 QAP, per DCA's board-approved substantive-changes summary). Up to 50% of the fee may be deferred, repayable within 15 years from cash flow.
fee.basis: Total development cost excluding developer fee and reserves (land included)
fee.dollarCap: $2,700,000 per development; $38,000 per unit (one Draft 2 excerpt showed $30,000 per unit; either way the $2.7M cap binds for the example)
fee.quote: 9% credits, new construction: lesser of 13% of total development cost (excluding developer fee and reserves), $2,700,000, or $38,000 per unit (search excerpt of DCA 2026-2027 QAP substantive changes, Draft 2 'updated the maximum developer fee calculations'). Full adopted QAP text could not be opened: https://dca.georgia.gov/document/document/2026-2027-qapboard-approvedpdf/download

maxFeasibleUnits.evidence: 2025 9% award list (announced Sept 23, 2025) includes RHA Redevelopment Phase II in Roswell (metro Atlanta), a 102-unit family new construction project. No QAP unit cap was found. Typical 9% awards are smaller: 31 developments / 1,983 units in 2025 (about 64 units each); Atlanta NC awards that year were 70, 50 and 42 units.

sponsorPath.evidence: QAP 'Experience, Capacity and Performance Requirements for General Partner and Developer Entities' rates developers (Qualified / Probationary). DCA text: it 'generally encourages entities that have insufficient technical expertise and/or experience to partner with Certifying Entities to gain experience and capacity in the Tax Credit program' and 'may, but is not required to, grant a waiver of development/credit award limitations for the proposed certifying partner.' Limits: 'Applicants either qualified as probationary or with minimal development experience (determined by DCA) are limited to one award per competitive round.' Read from search excerpts of QAP drafts (2024-2025 and 2026-2027 Draft 1), not the adopted text.

financingPath.evidence: Annual competitive 9% round funds mostly new construction: 2024 round 30 awards (post-reconsideration), 23 New Supply and 7 Preservation, $31.8M credits; 2025 round $37.2M for 31 developments. DCA reports a geographic split of 35% rural, 35% other metro, 30% metro Atlanta (2023 impact report). Note: Georgia HB 1199 caps aggregate annual state credits (9% and 4%) at $100M.

9%.nextDeadline: 2026 round: pre-application Feb 27, 2026; competitive application May 8, 2026 (closed). 2027 9% deadline not found; DCA rounds typically open in spring, awards Sept-Oct.

access.evidence: A documented partner path exists: DCA encourages less-experienced entities to partner with Certifying Entities and may waive award limits for the certifying partner. New/probationary applicants are limited to one award per round, and all applicants to a capped number of selected projects per round. Metro Atlanta receives about 30% of awards. Scoring details for a 100+ unit Atlanta deal were not reviewed.

urban.evidence: Atlanta supports large LIHTC buildings (e.g. Herndon Square Phase III 178 units, Bedford Pines 159, Folio House 149 bond-financed), but 9% awards average about 64 units and the $2.7M fee cap and roughly $1.2M average credit per award make a 100+ unit 9% deal hard; the largest 2025 9% NC award found was 102 units. No rent/vacancy data gathered (search budget exhausted).

execution.evidence: Atlanta is a direct short flight from Chicago; no local-presence rule found in excerpts; a Certifying Entity partner route exists. Partnering with local co-developers (e.g. Atlanta Housing teams) is common on large Atlanta deals.

fee.rule: 4% Credits/Bonds new construction: developer fee limited to the lesser of 13% of total development cost (excluding developer fee and all reserves) or $4,500,000 (2026-2027 QAP per DCA substantive-changes summary). One garbled Draft 2 excerpt also listed '$30,000 per unit' for 4%; if that applies the fee would be $3,600,000.
fee.basis: Total development cost excluding developer fee and all reserves (land included)
fee.quote: For 4% Credits/Bonds: New construction developments are limited to the lesser of 13% of total development cost (excluding developer fee and all reserves), $4,500,000 (search excerpt; another excerpt of the same document continued ', $30,000 per unit')

maxFeasibleUnits.evidence: Herndon Square Phase III (Atlanta, English Avenue/Westside), 178 units, closed financing March 2025 with Georgia DCA 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits (Pennrose, Atlanta Housing, Hunt Companies). The 2024 4% round drew 71 applications totaling 10,434 units (about 147 units each). No unit cap found.

sponsorPath.evidence: Same Certifying Entity partner path as 9%. 2023 QAP changes summary: 'probationary developers with experience comparable to fully qualified developers are permitted to be the Certifying Entity for 4% Credits/Bonds applications.' (search excerpt)

financingPath.evidence: DCA runs an annual competitive 4% Credits/Bonds round: $385,000,000 of bonds reserved for 4% awards in the 2025 round example, including a $123.2M Urban Housing Reservation for local urban residential finance authorities (e.g. Invest Atlanta). 2024 housing share of bond cap $585.9M; DCA projected $700M+ capacity and 26-30 awards. Competitive but not a multi-year waitlist. Per-application bond request capped (board-approved figure reported as $25M; drafts said $40M) which may constrain a 120-unit deal. DCA will reclaim excess volume under the new 25% test.

4%.nextDeadline: 2026 4% round competitive applications reported due Sept 25, 2026 (unconfirmed secondary source); 2025 deadline was Aug 1, 2025. Next round likely mid/late 2027 (not stated).

access.evidence: Partner path with a Certifying Entity is documented; probationary developers with comparable experience can be Certifying Entity on 4% deals. Round is scored and ranked and about 2.5x oversubscribed; Invest Atlanta (urban reservation) is a second route to bonds in Atlanta.

urban.evidence: Multiple 100+ unit new-construction bond/4% deals in Atlanta's Westside and downtown (Herndon Square Phase III 178 units; The Simpson 139 units, Vine City; Bedford Pines 159 units; Folio House 149 units) show rents and costs plausibly support 100+ unit LIHTC buildings. No vacancy or rent-gap data gathered.

execution.evidence: Reachable from Chicago; partner route exists; DCA warns it 'will be less flexible on developments awarded 4% Housing Credits/Bonds going forward' and advises not to apply with a financing gap, raising the capital/guarantee burden.

venture.market: Atlanta: Westside (English Avenue / Vine City, near Mercedes-Benz Stadium and downtown)

historicSuccess.evidence: Historic in-town neighborhoods adjacent to downtown, 'in the shadow of Mercedes-Benz Stadium', with long-standing infrastructure; long-disinvested, residents 'have long called for investment'.

anchorInstitutions.evidence: Mercedes-Benz Stadium and Georgia Tech nearby (a 170-unit LIHTC build near Georgia Tech was nearing opening); Westside Future Fund (civic/corporate-backed) actively investing. Specific university/hospital commitments to these blocks were not documented in my searches.

availableProperty.evidence: Westside Future Fund plans to 'transform vacant land in the English Avenue neighborhood' (Sunset Avenue, $2.5M TAD); Herndon Square phases redeveloping the former Herndon Homes site. Displacement concerns noted by WFF ('Restoration Without Displacement').

emergingMomentum.evidence: May 2025 Invest Atlanta Westside TAD awards for 166 units (150 affordable at 30-80% AMI), incl. $2.5M for 172 Vine Street; WFF's $48M North+Oliver, 'largest new affordable housing development in English Avenue in over a generation'; Herndon Square Phase III closed March 2025; Fulton County approved Vine City / English Avenue developments (Sept 2026).

localLeadership.evidence: Mayor Dickens' $5.1 billion plan 'centers around Thomasville Heights, English Avenue/Vine City, Grove Park/Bankhead'; Invest Atlanta (Westside TAD, Urban Residential Finance Authority bonds), Atlanta Housing and Westside Future Fund are identifiable implementing leaders.
